articles.title: Self-esteem provides no buffer against the stigma of commercial sex work
articles.summary: A recent survey of 310 commercial sex workers reveals that the mental health impacts of societal stigma are so severe that even high self-esteem offers no psychological protection against them.

articles.title: Plant-based compounds in berries and tea may help delay brain aging
articles.summary: A new scientific review suggests that polyphenols—natural compounds found in berries, tea, and olive oil—may help protect the brain from age-related decline. However, researchers emphasize eating whole foods over relying on high-dose supplements.

articles.title: Anxiety and feelings of entrapment may connect psychotic distress to suicidal ideation
articles.summary: A new study reveals that the emotional distress caused by hallucinations and delusions is strongly linked to suicidal thoughts. This connection operates through severe anxiety and feelings of entrapment, highlighting the importance of easing a person's subjective emotional pain.

articles.title: Oral GLP-1 drugs may quiet the brain’s food craving circuit
articles.summary: Newer oral drugs related to semaglutide medications such as Ozempic reduced pleasure-driven eating in mice by quieting a deep brain reward circuit. The finding could open new avenues for understanding food cravings and potentially treating substance use disorder.

articles.title: A single dose reversed autism-like symptoms in adult mice within hours
articles.summary: Even mild inflammation during pregnancy led mouse offspring to develop persistent brain overactivity, sensory sensitivity, repetitive behaviors, and increased seizure risk. Remarkably, one dose of rapamycin improved nearly all of these problems within about two hours. The benefits were temporary, but they suggest that adult brain circuits may remain far more adaptable than previously believed.

articles.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
articles.summary: Scientists expected SuperAgers might simply inherit fewer Alzheimer’s-related risks, but their genes looked much like those of typical older adults. Their extraordinary memories may instead come from still-unknown protective forces involving the brain, body, lifestyle, and environment.

articles.title: Lab-grown mini brains may predict which Alzheimer’s treatments will work
articles.summary: Miniature brain models grown from patients’ cells revealed striking differences in how Alzheimer’s-related tissue responds to an antidepressant. The organoids and the particles they release could eventually guide more personalized treatments and provide new clues for diagnosing the disease.

articles.title: Aphantasia is linked to specific face recognition deficits, but matching skills remain intact
articles.summary: A new study reveals that individuals with aphantasia experience specific deficits in perceiving and remembering faces. However, their ability to visually match faces remains intact, highlighting the complex nature of facial recognition.

articles.summary: If you have a genetic risk for depression, the hardest part of a breakup might be the years leading up to it. A new study found these individuals showed increased antidepressant use years before their relationships actually ended.

articles.summary: A new study reveals that mirror neurons don’t just care about final goals. Instead, these brain cells work together in dynamic networks to continuously track the specific physical details of observed movements in real time.

articles.title: Watching too much TV in midlife may shrink the brain
articles.summary: Watching television very often in midlife may be linked to troubling brain changes decades later. In a study of about 1,700 adults, frequent TV viewers later showed smaller brain regions involved in memory, decision-making, and visual processing, along with more signs of damage in the brain’s white matter. Surprisingly, sitting itself did not appear to be the main issue, since people who spent long hours seated at mentally engaging jobs often showed healthier brain patterns.
